newsletter.subject: Sea of red: crypto slides with stocks (here's what I'm watching)
newsletter.preview: BTC is back near $81.7K. No crypto-specific trigger, just a global risk-off day. Levels, paper trades, and what's next.
newsletter.tldr: Almost everything is down today. Bitcoin is around $81,700 (-2.1% in 24h) and alts are off 2-9%. No crypto-specific trigger has been reported; crypto is moving with a global risk-off mood driven by AI-spending doubts, falling Asian stocks and higher oil.
what_happened: **Stocks wobbled first.** Tesla cut its capital-spending forecast and Lam Research fell 7% on a weak outlook, reviving doubts about AI spending. Nasdaq 100 futures slid almost 2% ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/22/bitcoin-gives-back-its-run-at-usd85-000-as-tesla-and-meta-fail-to-calm-ai-nerves)).

**Asia fell hard.** The Nikkei, Kospi and Hang Seng each dropped about 3% or more, and China's CSI 300 is now 20% off its June peak, which puts it in a bear market. Brent crude topped $112 on Middle East tensions ([CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/22/asian-stocks-tumble-bitcoin-retreats-as-china-enters-bear-market)).

**BTC gave back its breakout.** It topped near $84,850 late Wednesday, then slid back under the $82,500 level many analysts watch. One bright spot: spot BTC ETFs have taken in $1.1B net so far this week ([Moneycontrol/Bloomberg](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/cryptocurrency/bitcoin-falls-below-83-000-as-ai-jitters-weigh-on-sentiment-14057385.html)).
**Noise, not news:** a widely shared FBI warning about PHP vulnerabilities is a web-server issue, not a blockchain one.
levels: **BTC ~$81,700:** under $82,500. Next supports $81,000, then $80,000. It needs to get back above $82,500 first; $84,850 is the ceiling.
**HBAR ~$0.0807 (-4.7%):** lost $0.082 and $0.0814; $0.080 is the floor. Reclaim $0.082 to steady.
**XRP ~$1.325 (-2.5%):** just under the $1.33 pivot; next $1.29. Needs $1.37 to turn up.
**ZBCN ~$0.00224:** testing $0.00224 support; $0.00219 is the line under it.
**AXL ~$0.0488 (-8.6%):** worst on the list (low $0.0482). The $0.0475 floor is the last stop of its range.
**XDC ~$0.0348:** holding up best, on $0.0347 support; $0.0339 below, $0.036 ceiling.
whats_next: **Wed, Oct 28:** Fed decision. Expect choppy, headline-driven trading until then.

**The yen:** USD/JPY dropped from about 158.2 to about 157 overnight (stronger yen) ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/USDJPY%3DX/history/)). In Aug 2024, a fast yen surge (roughly 161 to 142) forced a carry-trade unwind and crypto crashed. This move is much smaller, but I'm watching ~155.

items.headline: Ripple and Arf bring RLUSD settlement loans to the XRP Ledger
items.summary: Swiss settlement firm Arf partnered with Ripple to lend the RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger as short-term working capital for licensed cross-border payment companies. No launch date has been set.
items.why: That brings real payment settlement to the XRP Ledger.

items.headline: First institutional repo trade completes on Stellar
items.summary: Ascend Markets and M1X Global completed the first institutional repo trade on Stellar, backed by a Treasury-secured token, with 72 automated hourly rolls including overnight and the weekend.
items.why: It shows Stellar running round-the-clock secured financing, not just payments.

items.headline: SEC crypto rule comments close with Ripple urging adoption
items.summary: comments closed on the SEC's proposed crypto asset rules. Ripple supported the proposal with changes, while state regulators asked the SEC to withdraw it.
items.why: The final rule will shape how XRP, XLM and HBAR trade in the U.S.

items.headline: OCC stablecoin rule under the GENIUS Act hits the Federal Register
items.summary: the OCC's stablecoin rule under the GENIUS Act was published in the Federal Register today. It takes effect January 18, 2027.
items.why: That sets federal ground rules for dollar stablecoins like RLUSD and USDC.
